source.title: Fighting the Horde: a Comprehensive Model for Monitoring and Controlling Hornet Invasions

source_quality.summary: All 25 pages were read and visually reconciled. The source contains current-nest inference, AHP habitat weighting, next-year spread, hybrid image labeling, ResNet domain failure and task downgrade, piecewise priority queues, paired reranking, trigger-based updating, a modified sighting-gap signal, source-specific limitations, a memorandum and code.

decisions: what officers and beekeepers should do

title: Fighting the Horde: a Comprehensive Model for Monitoring and Controlling Hornet Invasions
unresolved_questions: The Summary's almost-98% claim refers to binary overall accuracy, not 13-class citizen-photo performance.
The Summary's eradication language is stronger than the evidence supplied by the altered sighting-gap formula.
Most citizen reports being mistaken is asserted without a source-level denominator in the prose.
Finite agency resources are not quantified as staff, hours, service times or budget.
Overseas hornet cases do not determine Washington spread or detection performance.
Expert labels are assumed error-free, so label uncertainty is excluded by construction.
Constant public attentiveness is implausible under media cycles, interventions and seasonal concern.
The claim that nonnegative patrol distance justifies a Poisson distribution is mathematically insufficient.
Poisson distance uses a count distribution on a quantity presented as continuous geographic distance.
Patrol averages and maxima are not converted into a calibrated distance likelihood.
The 10 km current-nest search radius is not reconciled with the stated 8 km maximum patrol distance.
Summing sighting influence values produces a report-count-dependent surface and is not normalized as a posterior.
Confirmed sightings can share a colony, so treating each influence independently can double count evidence.
Tree coverage and elevation are visually asserted to coincide but not measured.
Elevation is used as both terrain and forest proxy, confounding two ecological mechanisms.
Min-max elevation normalization depends on the selected local bounding area.
AHP pairwise judgments are subjective and lack alternative-matrix sensitivity.
`CR<0.10` tests matrix consistency, not ecological validity or predictive accuracy.
The AHP map is shown without a held-out discovered-nest check.
The 30 km annual queen movement is treated as a distribution center without uncertainty.
The spread model appears to reuse the current-nest kernel without a full state-transition derivation.
The next-year map is not compared with observed future nests.
Excluding unverified and unprocessed records selects cases with easier evidence and may bias the classifier.
NLP noun extraction and manual mapping to 13 species lack an annotation protocol and agreement check.
External bugguide images can contain curation, copyright, duplicate and label-selection effects.
Exactly 200 external images per species imposes an artificial class composition.
The relationship between supplied, downloaded, cropped, training and evaluation image counts is not fully reconciled.
The one-tenth evaluation split has no seed, stratification or grouping by source/duplicate identity.
Website and citizen images can leak near duplicates or photographer-specific patterns across the split.
ResNet pretrained weights, library versions and preprocessing environment are not frozen.
Accuracy alone is inadequate for a rare, safety-relevant target class.
No target recall, precision, specificity, F1, ROC/PR curve or calibrated probability is reported.
The 13-class uploaded-photo accuracies of 12.64-19.83% show severe domain failure.
The explanation based on blur, centering and resolution is plausible but not experimentally isolated.
Manual cropping all target images can introduce label-aware processing bias.
The cropped set has only 107 images and contains all Asian giant hornet pictures, making class balance atypical.
Cropping raises the best multiclass value only to 27.10%, still far below website performance.
The proposed pixel-loss explanation after cropping is not tested against sharpening or higher-resolution capture.
Switching from 13 classes to binary changes the task and cannot be presented as improving the same classifier objective.
Binary overall accuracy near 98% is dominated by the many non-target reports.
The source itself notes that only a few of more than one thousand report images are target-class.
The confusion matrix is not accompanied by raw counts, normalized-axis declaration or target-class rates.
Target hornets are visibly confused with fly, normal hornet and bee, creating false-negative risk.
Cicada killers are confused with the target, creating avoidable expert workload.
CNN output values are treated as probabilities without calibration evidence.
The credibility score combines components with different, uncalibrated meanings.
The 20 km and 70 km group thresholds have no empirical or operational derivation.
The 60/40 and 50/20/30 weights have no fitting, elicitation or sensitivity analysis.
Geographic distance to a previous sighting is not equivalent to distance from a true nest.
The Poisson term `2^d/d! exp(-2)` becomes numerically inappropriate for non-integer kilometer distance and large d.
The source defines `p_nest` but uses `p_next` in the Group 1 credibility equation.
Deleting photos below `c_sight<0.01` has no false-negative quarantine, audit or appeal path.
Group staffing proportions are ordered but not numerically assigned.
Empty-queue reallocation lacks service-time, concurrency and arrival-process analysis.
The 268 km example demonstrates routing, not score calibration or overall effectiveness.
The classifier example emits a cicada-killer label but no decision confidence boundary.
The 1,400-photo reranking reuses previously verified records and is not a sealed prospective test.
Only five positives support the dramatic ranking-improvement claim.
The ranking test does not report how many negatives are promoted ahead of positives or the manual hours saved.
The model's benefit under backlog is qualitative because the workload crossover is not simulated.
Adding every expert-labeled photo to training can reinforce correlated label or source errors.
Annual deletion of previous nest data may discard information useful for dispersal history and reporting bias.
Update rules lack retraining cadence, validation gates, versioning, rollback, drift alarms and owners.
The original Solow-Roberts expression is altered without proving the modified indicator remains a probability.
The average second-difference term can be negative and can move the final ratio outside a meaningful probability range.
Sighting intervals reflect observation effort, traps, media attention and intervention as well as true survival.
The May-November window does not correct for changing spatial coverage or detection probability.
`p<0.05` cannot demonstrate eradication under imperfect detection and unobserved nests.
The memorandum strengthens weak binary accuracy and eradication evidence while omitting their main caveats.
Figure 13 is an illustrative interface, not evidence of deployment, usability, accessibility or live self-improvement.

Excluding unverified and unprocessed records selects cases with easier evidence and may bias the classifier.
NLP noun extraction and manual mapping to 13 species lack an annotation protocol and agreement check.
External bugguide images can contain curation, copyright, duplicate and label-selection effects.
Exactly 200 external images per species imposes an artificial class composition.
The relationship between supplied, downloaded, cropped, training and evaluation image counts is not fully reconciled.
The one-tenth evaluation split has no seed, stratification or grouping by source/duplicate identity.
Website and citizen images can leak near duplicates or photographer-specific patterns across the split.
ResNet pretrained weights, library versions and preprocessing environment are not frozen.
Accuracy alone is inadequate for a rare, safety-relevant target class.
No target recall, precision, specificity, F1, ROC/PR curve or calibrated probability is reported.
The 13-class uploaded-photo accuracies of 12.64-19.83% show severe domain failure.
The explanation based on blur, centering and resolution is plausible but not experimentally isolated.
Manual cropping all target images can introduce label-aware processing bias.
The cropped set has only 107 images and contains all Asian giant hornet pictures, making class balance atypical.
Cropping raises the best multiclass value only to 27.10%, still far below website performance.
The proposed pixel-loss explanation after cropping is not tested against sharpening or higher-resolution capture.
Switching from 13 classes to binary changes the task and cannot be presented as improving the same classifier objective.
Binary overall accuracy near 98% is dominated by the many non-target reports.
The source itself notes that only a few of more than one thousand report images are target-class.
The confusion matrix is not accompanied by raw counts, normalized-axis declaration or target-class rates.
Target hornets are visibly confused with fly, normal hornet and bee, creating false-negative risk.
Cicada killers are confused with the target, creating avoidable expert workload.
CNN output values are treated as probabilities without calibration evidence.
The credibility score combines components with different, uncalibrated meanings.
The 20 km and 70 km group thresholds have no empirical or operational derivation.
The 60/40 and 50/20/30 weights have no fitting, elicitation or sensitivity analysis.
Geographic distance to a previous sighting is not equivalent to distance from a true nest.
The Poisson term `2^d/d! exp(-2)` becomes numerically inappropriate for non-integer kilometer distance and large d.
The source defines `p_nest` but uses `p_next` in the Group 1 credibility equation.
Deleting photos below `c_sight<0.01` has no false-negative quarantine, audit or appeal path.
Group staffing proportions are ordered but not numerically assigned.
Empty-queue reallocation lacks service-time, concurrency and arrival-process analysis.
The 268 km example demonstrates routing, not score calibration or overall effectiveness.
The classifier example emits a cicada-killer label but no decision confidence boundary.
The 1,400-photo reranking reuses previously verified records and is not a sealed prospective test.
Only five positives support the dramatic ranking-improvement claim.
The ranking test does not report how many negatives are promoted ahead of positives or the manual hours saved.
The model's benefit under backlog is qualitative because the workload crossover is not simulated.
Adding every expert-labeled photo to training can reinforce correlated label or source errors.
Annual deletion of previous nest data may discard information useful for dispersal history and reporting bias.
Update rules lack retraining cadence, validation gates, versioning, rollback, drift alarms and owners.
The original Solow-Roberts expression is altered without proving the modified indicator remains a probability.
The average second-difference term can be negative and can move the final ratio outside a meaningful probability range.
Sighting intervals reflect observation effort, traps, media attention and intervention as well as true survival.
The May-November window does not correct for changing spatial coverage or detection probability.
`p<0.05` cannot demonstrate eradication under imperfect detection and unobserved nests.
The memorandum strengthens weak binary accuracy and eradication evidence while omitting their main caveats.
Figure 13 is an illustrative interface, not evidence of deployment, usability, accessibility or live self-improvement.
